questions.q: What will be the magnitude of the electric field at point O as shown in the figure? Each side of the figure is l and perpendicular to the other?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the point $O$ be the origin $(0,0)$ of a Cartesian coordinate system.

The positions and magnitudes of the charges are: $q_B = +q$ at $(-l, 0)$, $q_G = +2q$ at $(l, 0)$, $q_F = +q$ at $(0, -l)$, $q_A = -q$ at $(-l, l)$, $q_D = +q$ at $(l, l)$, $q_E = +2q$ at $(-l, -l)$, and $q_H = -q$ at $(l, -l)$.

Let $E_0 = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q}{l^2}$.

The electric field contributions at the origin from the charges on the axes are:
$\vec{E}_B = E_0 \hat{i}$
$\vec{E}_G = -2E_0 \hat{i}$
$\vec{E}_F = E_0 \hat{j}$

The net electric field from these axial charges is:
$\vec{E}_{axial} = \vec{E}_B + \vec{E}_G + \vec{E}_F = -E_0 \hat{i} + E_0 \hat{j}$

The distance of all corner charges from the origin is $\sqrt{l^2 + l^2} = l\sqrt{2}$. The electric field contributions at the origin from the corner charges are:
$\vec{E}_A = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q}{(l\sqrt{2})^2} \left( \dfrac{-\hat{i} + \hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}} \right) = \dfrac{E_0}{2\sqrt{2}} (-\hat{i} + \hat{j})$
$\vec{E}_D = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q}{(l\sqrt{2})^2} \left( \dfrac{-\hat{i} - \hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}} \right) = \dfrac{E_0}{2\sqrt{2}} (-\hat{i} - \hat{j})$
$\vec{E}_E = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{2q}{(l\sqrt{2})^2} \left( \dfrac{\hat{i} + \hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}} \right) = \dfrac{2E_0}{2\sqrt{2}} (\hat{i} + \hat{j})$
$\vec{E}_H = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q}{(l\sqrt{2})^2} \left( \dfrac{\hat{i} - \hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}} \right) = \dfrac{E_0}{2\sqrt{2}} (\hat{i} - \hat{j})$

The net electric field from the diagonal charges is:
$\vec{E}_{diag} = \vec{E}_A + \vec{E}_D + \vec{E}_E + \vec{E}_H$
$\vec{E}_{diag} = \dfrac{E_0}{2\sqrt{2}} [ (-\hat{i} + \hat{j}) + (-\hat{i} - \hat{j}) + 2(\hat{i} + \hat{j}) + (\hat{i} - \hat{j}) ]$
$\vec{E}_{diag} = \dfrac{E_0}{2\sqrt{2}} [ (-1 - 1 + 2 + 1)\hat{i} + (1 - 1 + 2 - 1)\hat{j} ] = \dfrac{E_0}{2\sqrt{2}} (\hat{i} + \hat{j})$

The total electric field at the origin is $\vec{E}_{net} = \vec{E}_{axial} + \vec{E}_{diag}$:
$\vec{E}_{net} = (-E_0 \hat{i} + E_0 \hat{j}) + \dfrac{E_0}{2\sqrt{2}} (\hat{i} + \hat{j}) = E_0 \left( \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} - 1 \right) \hat{i} + E_0 \left( \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} + 1 \right) \hat{j}$

The magnitude of the net electric field is:
$|\vec{E}_{net}| = E_0 \sqrt{ \left( \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} - 1 \right)^2 + \left( \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} + 1 \right)^2 }$
$|\vec{E}_{net}| = E_0 \sqrt{ \left( \dfrac{1}{8} - \dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{2}} + 1 \right) + \left( \dfrac{1}{8} + \dfrac{2}{2\sqrt{2}} + 1 \right) }$
$|\vec{E}_{net}| = E_0 \sqrt{ \dfrac{2}{8} + 2 } = E_0 \sqrt{ 2.25 }$
$|\vec{E}_{net}| = 1.5 E_0 = \dfrac{3}{2} E_0$

Substituting $E_0 = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q}{l^2}$ back into the expression:
$|\vec{E}_{net}| = \dfrac{3}{2} \left( \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{q}{l^2} \right)$

questions.q:
Electric potential at a point P due to a point charge of 5×10-9 C is 50 V. The distance of P from the point charge is:
(Assume, 14πε0=9×109 N m2 C-2)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The electric potential for a point charge is given by 

V=Q4πε0r

The data given is 

V=50 VQ=5×10-9 C

So, the distance of the point is 

 r=14πε0QV
⇒r=9×109×5×10-950
⇒r=0.9 m=90 cm

A very small point like piece of it of mass m gets detached from the bottom of the sphere and falls down vertically under gravity. This piece carries charge q. If it acquires a speed ν when it has fallen through a vertical height y (see figure), then (assume the remaining portion to be spherical)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
By using total energy conservation
ΔKE+(ΔPE)electo +(ΔPE)gravitation =0

12mV2+kQqR+y-kQqR+(-mgy)=0

12mV2=mgy+kQq1R-1R+y;  V2=2gy+2kQqmyR(R+y)

V2=2yqQ4πε0R(R+y)m+g

The whole system is placed on a frictionless horizontal plane and is initially at rest. If uniform electric field is switched on along the direction as shown in figure, then the speed of the particle when it crosses the x -axis is

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{all}}=\Delta \mathrm{k} \\ & \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{e}}=\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{f}}-\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{i}} \\ & \mathrm{qE} \frac{\ell}{2}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2-0 \\ & \mathrm{v}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{qE} \ell}{\mathrm{m}}}\end{aligned}$

The arrangement is now placed near an infinite nonconducting charge sheet with uniform charge density of $100 \mu \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}^2$ such that length of rod makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with electric field generated by charge sheet. Net torque acting on the rod is:
(Take $\varepsilon_0: 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{C}^2 / \mathrm{Nm}^2$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{E} & =\frac{\sigma}{2 \varepsilon_0} \\ \tau & =\mathrm{PE} \sin \theta\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned} & =\left[\left(2 \times 10^{-6}\right)\left(\frac{2}{10}\right)\right]\left[\frac{100 \times 10^{-6}}{2 \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12}}\right]\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \\ & =\frac{10}{8.85}=1.12 \mathrm{Nm}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The electric field due to a short electric dipole at a large distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mi>r</mi></mfenced></math> from center of dipole on the equatorial plane varies with distance as :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
An electric dipole is a system of two charges of equal and opposite magnitude placed at a short distance.

The dipole moment is, p=2ql.

The electric field due to the dipole is,

E=2kpr3

Clearly, the electric field varies as 1r3.

questions.q: Two uniformly charged spherical conductors <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> of radii <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> are separated by a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. If the spheres are connected by a conducting wire, then in equilibrium condition, the ratio of the magnitudes of the electric fields at the surface of the sphere <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When two conductors are connected by a conducting wire, their potentials become equal. Therefore, VA=VB

The potential of a spherical conductor is given by, V=kQR

⇒kQARA=kQBRB

⇒Q∝R

Now the electric field near the surface of the conductor will be, E=kQR2

⇒EAEB=kQARA2kQBRB2=RBRA

⇒EAEB=105=21

questions.q: An electric field of $1000 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{m}$ is applied to an electric dipole at angle of $45^{\circ}$. The value of electric dipole moment is $10^{-29} \mathrm{C} \cdot \mathrm{m} .$ What is the potential energy of the electric dipole?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Potential energy of a dipole is given by $\mathrm{U}=-\overrightarrow{\mathrm{P}} \overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}=-P E \cos \theta$

[Where $\theta=$ angle between dipole and perpendicular to the field $=-\left(10^{-29}\right)\left(10^{3}\right) \cos 45^{\circ}=-0.707 \times 10^{-26} \mathrm{~J}=-7 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{~J}$

questions.q: A two point charges 4q and –q are fixed on the x -axis at x=−d2 and x=d2, respectively. If the third point charge ‘q ’ is taken from the origin to x=d along the semicircle as shown in the figure, the energy of the charge will:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Potential at origin O, the potential due to two charges is given by

V0=4q4πε0d2+−q4πε0d2=6q4πε0d

Potential at P at a distance, x=d is given by

VP=4q4πε03d2+−q4πε0d2=q6πε0d

Change in potential energy due the charge motion of charge q is given by

 ∆U=qΔV=qVf−Vi

⇒∆U=qVP−VO

∆U=qq6πε0d−3q2πε0d=−4q23πε0d

In this situation, the position of the proton from the origin is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let at point P net electric field is zero.

As direction of electric field due to both charges at point P is opposite, equating magnitude we get

14πε04q0x2=14πε0q0x-122⇒2x-12=x⇒x=24 cm

Distance of proton from origin =24 cm.
